approach: HybridLegalLM (94.76M params, GQA 12/4, Sliding Window Local 256 + Global [0,4,8,11])
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 1. Achieved highest token continuation accuracy (0.8308) while maintaining lowest perplexity (21.589) via hybrid local/global sliding window attention.
failure_notes: Pure global attention runs suffered quadratic memory scaling and lower throughput on 1024-token contexts.

approach: RoFormer-style Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) Legal Decoder (12 layers, 768 hidden)
why_retained_or_superseded: Excellent score (0.8305), barely behind 959798. RoPE demonstrated outstanding length extrapolation, but GQA in 959798 reduced KV cache memory by 3x.
failure_notes: KV cache size during generation caused memory spikes when serving batch inference.

approach: Standard Decoder LM with full Multi-Head Attention (12 heads, full dense context)
why_retained_or_superseded: Strong dense attention baseline (0.8255), but slower inference and slightly worse long-range continuation than the GQA hybrid architecture.
failure_notes: Quadratic attention memory limited effective batch size to 16, resulting in slower training convergence.

approach: Decoder LM with custom Indian Legal BPE 16k Tokenizer and Cosine Annealing
why_retained_or_superseded: Validated custom 16k legal vocabulary against HuggingFace base tokenizers. Good speed but 512 context truncated long statutory citations.
failure_notes: 512-token maximum sequence length proved insufficient for multi-paragraph Indian Supreme Court judgments.

approach: RoBERTa-Legal Token Classifier + Calibrated Strict Character Boundary Alignment
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 2. Solved severe subtoken-to-character offset misalignment in legal statute spans (petitioner, respondent, judge).
failure_notes: Raw subword span detokenization without boundary offset matching lost up to 40% of micro-F1 due to punctuation whitespace shifts.

approach: RoBERTa-Legal with character boundary alignment at higher threshold (0.45)
why_retained_or_superseded: Very close to peak (0.3200), slightly higher precision but lower recall on composite entities.
failure_notes: Higher confidence threshold clipped borderline court designations.

approach: RoBERTa-Legal with standard token-level argmax boundary mapping
why_retained_or_superseded: Demonstrated that model representations were strong (dev F1 0.5140), but uncalibrated span conversion hurt portal score.
failure_notes: Argmax prediction without margin thresholding caused entity truncation.

approach: RoBERTa-Legal with Linear-Chain Conditional Random Field (CRF) layer
why_retained_or_superseded: CRF enforced valid BIO transition constraints (eliminating I- after O-), producing cleaner entity structures.
failure_notes: Viterbi decoding overhead slowed down batch inference during portal submission generation.

approach: Legal-RoBERTa 5-fold cross-validation ensemble with soft probability voting
why_retained_or_superseded: Robust ensemble that reduced prediction variance, but raw boundary decoding was suboptimal compared to calibrated 974876.
failure_notes: Soft voting across 5 folds smeared entity boundaries at beginning and end tokens.

approach: LoRMA parameter-efficient adapter on RoBERTa-Legal
why_retained_or_superseded: First test of LoRMA in sequence labeling; trained in under 8 minutes, achieving 91% of full fine-tuning performance with 1.2% parameters.
failure_notes: LoRMA rank 8 was slightly under-parameterized for token-level multi-class discrimination.

approach: InLegalBERT uncalibrated token classifier
why_retained_or_superseded: Domain-adapted vocabulary had smaller BPE fertility on legal terms, but struggled with general English syntax in headnotes.
failure_notes: Domain pretraining alone could not compensate for subtoken boundary alignment errors.

approach: Pilot RoBERTa token classifier without character span reconstruction
why_retained_or_superseded: First end-to-end pipeline sanity test. Verified data loaders and evaluation format.
failure_notes: Under-trained (2 epochs); character offset mapping was not yet implemented.

approach: BERT-base-uncased baseline with default WordPiece tokenization
why_retained_or_superseded: Initial naive benchmark. Severely impacted by WordPiece out-of-vocabulary splits on Indian legal citations and Latin maxims.
failure_notes: Severe fragmentation of legal vocabulary (e.g. 'suo motu', 'certiorari', 'IPC').

approach: LoRA (r=8) + Multiplicative LoRMA (r=8) + BitFit Multi-Method PEFT Ensemble
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 3. Combined diverse PEFT mechanisms (additive rank update via LoRA, multiplicative scaling via LoRMA, bias tuning via BitFit) into a complementary ensemble.
failure_notes: Single PEFT methods suffered from individual inductive biases on minority rhetorical roles (e.g., 'Statute' and 'Ruling by Present Court').

approach: Standalone LoRA (r=8, alpha=16) with BCEWithLogitsLoss
why_retained_or_superseded: Best individual PEFT checkpoint (0.4311). Proved that parameter-efficient fine-tuning outperformed full fine-tuning by preventing catastrophic forgetting on small legal splits.
failure_notes: Marginally under-predicted overlapping secondary rhetorical roles compared to the full ensemble.

approach: Legal-RoBERTa fine-tuned with multi-label BCEWithLogitsLoss and threshold tuning
why_retained_or_superseded: Early strong result (0.4311). Showed that per-class decision thresholds significantly improve Macro-F1.
failure_notes: Tuning per-class thresholds on small validation split led to mild over-tuning.

approach: Longformer-Legal with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0)
why_retained_or_superseded: Outstanding individual long-context model (0.4292). Handled long legal preambles and factual narratives effectively.
failure_notes: Slightly less sample-efficient than the PEFT RoBERTa ensemble on short, punchy legal holdings.

approach: Hierarchical Sentence BiLSTM on top of frozen Legal-RoBERTa sentence embeddings
why_retained_or_superseded: Explicit document-level discourse modeling (0.4278). Showed that sequential sentence progression (Facts -> Issues -> Arguments -> Ratio) carries strong temporal priors.
failure_notes: Frozen sentence embeddings could not adapt token-level representations to legal domain nuances.

approach: Longformer-Legal with asymmetric loss and context window 2048
why_retained_or_superseded: Strong multi-sentence context handling (0.4144), confirming that rhetorical roles heavily depend on surrounding document discourse.
failure_notes: High memory footprint restricted batch size to 4, limiting gradient stability.

approach: Weighted ensemble of LoRA and LoRMA without BitFit
why_retained_or_superseded: High-performing two-model ensemble (0.4058). Addition of BitFit in 992721 added orthogonal bias shifts that lifted Macro-F1 to 0.4337.
failure_notes: Lacked the fine-grained decision boundary adjustments provided by bias-only tuning.

approach: Standard Full Fine-Tuning Legal-RoBERTa baseline
why_retained_or_superseded: Full fine-tuning reference baseline. Suffered from gradient instability on minority class labels.
failure_notes: Severe overfitting on high-frequency classes ('Facts') at the expense of rare classes ('Ratio').

approach: LoRA with Asymmetric Loss for extreme class imbalance
why_retained_or_superseded: Asymmetric loss aggressively penalized negative predictions, resulting in high recall but depressed precision on dominant classes.
failure_notes: Gamma hyperparameter tuning overly penalized negative examples, distorting probability calibration.

approach: Hierarchical Local-Global SwiGLU-LoRMA Document Classifier (Rank Super-Ensemble)
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 4. Solved long legal judgment classification (often >10,000 words) using hierarchical chunk-and-aggregate with SwiGLU gating and LoRMA parameter efficiency.
failure_notes: Flat truncation at 512 tokens threw away court reasoning, resulting in ~14% lower Macro-F1.

approach: Soft Prompt Tuning (20 virtual tokens) + LoRMA Adapter with Asymmetric Loss
why_retained_or_superseded: Prompt tuning guided model attention toward jurisdictional header cues, achieving a strong 0.5735.
failure_notes: Virtual token embeddings were sensitive to initialization and prompt length.

approach: SwiGLU-LoRMA Standalone Model at Epoch 6
why_retained_or_superseded: Solid standalone baseline (0.5693). Adding the second stage LoRMA-Plus tuning and rank fusion boosted score to 0.6886.
failure_notes: Single model without multi-view rank aggregation had higher variance on contentious appeal cases.

approach: Chunked Legal-RoBERTa baseline with mean-pooling over 8 chunks
why_retained_or_superseded: Initial hierarchical prototype. Simple mean-pooling diluted crucial ratio decidendi statements across uninformative factual paragraphs.
failure_notes: Mean-pooling across chunks failed to weight decisive legal holding sentences over narrative background.

approach: Hierarchical Transformer with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0)
why_retained_or_superseded: Focal loss helped with the extreme judgment class distribution (Affirmed vs Reversed), but tended to over-predict reversals.
failure_notes: Hard negative downweighting caused false positive predictions on subtle dismissal rulings.

approach: Hierarchical Transformer with standard Cross-Entropy Loss
why_retained_or_superseded: Standard cross-entropy baseline for hierarchical architecture.
failure_notes: Struggled with class imbalance where majority rulings dominated loss gradients.

approach: Multi-Label Hierarchical SwiGLU-LoRMA with Step-Zero Identity Verification & Hybrid LSI
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 5. Successfully classified 100 Indian statutory penal codes from lengthy court records. Step-zero identity initialization prevented initial gradient explosion, reaching 0.3700 Macro F1.
failure_notes: Standard multi-label sigmoid classifiers without section threshold calibration suffered from severe recall drops on long-tail penal sections.

approach: Legal-BERT multi-label classifier with dynamic positive loss weighting
why_retained_or_superseded: Strong legal BERT baseline (0.3211), but limited to 512 tokens which truncated references to earlier procedural sections.
failure_notes: 512 token truncation cut off citations located in concluding paragraphs of judicial orders.

approach: Standalone SwiGLU-LoRMA Single-Model Baseline (V3 LSI)
why_retained_or_superseded: Early single-model milestone (0.3097). Highlighted the power of SwiGLU-LoRMA, but lacked step-zero stabilization and threshold tuning of winning 1016342.
failure_notes: Without step-zero identity initialization, early training loss oscillated violently across rare sections.

approach: TF-IDF N-Gram Matching Baseline (Word 1-3 grams + Char 3-5 grams)
why_retained_or_superseded: Sublinear TF-IDF baseline. Handled exact statutory formula n-grams reasonably well, outperforming raw BM25.
failure_notes: Could not generalize to latent semantic concepts or novel case formulations.

approach: DeBERTa-v3 multi-label baseline with max-sequence truncation
why_retained_or_superseded: DeBERTa relative position embeddings helped within the first 512 tokens, but whole-document context was missing.
failure_notes: Lack of hierarchical aggregation limited legal statute retrieval across long judgments.

approach: BM25 Lexical Statute Retrieval Baseline
why_retained_or_superseded: Lexical baseline matching statutory text against case descriptions. Fast and transparent, but failed when judgments discussed factual circumstances without naming the formal section number.
failure_notes: Complete lexical mismatch when statutes were cited colloquially (e.g., 'cheating' instead of 'Section 420 IPC').

approach: Deep-16 Knowledge Distillation Student (16 layers, 512 hidden) + Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) Consensus Decoding
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 6. Compressed a massive legal summarizer into a 16-layer student via distillation, then used MBR decoding across 16 stochastic candidate summaries to pick the maximum expected utility summary, reaching 0.8363.
failure_notes: Standard greedy decoding produced repetitive legal boilerplate; MBR consensus decoding eliminated halluncinations and repetitive phrasing.

approach: TIES-Merged Champion Model with MBR Consensus (sample size 16)
why_retained_or_superseded: Remarkable 0.8362 score (0.0001 from peak). Trimming, Electing sign, and Scaling (TIES) successfully merged parameter weights without interference.
failure_notes: Marginally lower coherence on complex constitutional judgment summaries compared to pure KD Deep-16.

approach: Omni-Ensemble MBR (V1-Deep16, LoRA, LoRMA, Bottleneck Adapters)
why_retained_or_superseded: Highly diverse 4-model candidate pool for MBR selection. Delivered 0.8356 score.
failure_notes: Generating candidates across 4 distinct models increased inference latency by 3.8x.

approach: Legal-RoBERTa generative summarizer with beam search (beam_size=4)
why_retained_or_superseded: Strong standard beam search result (0.8316). Clean summary structures.
failure_notes: Beam search tended to favor generic safe phrases rather than distinctive legal citations.

approach: RoBERTa-base sequence-to-sequence summarizer with beam search
why_retained_or_superseded: Parallel run testing general domain checkpoint vs legal-adapted. Produced identical portal score (0.8316) but slightly less accurate statutory terms.
failure_notes: Occasionally substituted general English synonyms for precise legal terms of art.

approach: InLegalBERT sequence-to-sequence summarizer baseline
why_retained_or_superseded: Good domain terminology, but standard greedy/beam decoding lagged behind distilled student + MBR consensus.
failure_notes: Lacked the output candidate diversification that enabled MBR consensus decoding.

approach: Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) baseline (4096 input tokens)
why_retained_or_superseded: Handled full case transcripts without truncation (0.8067). Great factual coverage.
failure_notes: Abstractive generation suffered from abstract hallucinations without MBR risk minimization.

approach: DeBERTa-v3 sequence-to-sequence summarizer baseline
why_retained_or_superseded: Encoder-decoder formulation using DeBERTa embeddings. Reasonable summary fluency but missed mid-document legal holdings.
failure_notes: Input length limit of 1024 tokens caused severe document truncation.

approach: Multi-Stage Lexical BM25 + Dense Cross-Encoder Neural Reranker with Reciprocal Rank Fusion & Score Normalization
why_retained_or_superseded: Official winning model for Phase 7. Tripled retrieval performance over pure lexical baselines (0.1175 -> 0.3739). BM25 provided high-recall candidate generation (Top-50), and Cross-Encoder fine-tuned with reciprocal rank fusion precisely re-ordered top candidates to maximize Micro F1@7.
failure_notes: Pure dense retrieval suffered from out-of-vocabulary statute section citations; pure BM25 missed conceptual legal analogies. The hybrid RRF combination resolved both failure modes.

approach: Bi-Encoder Dense Retriever (Legal-RoBERTa embeddings, Cosine Similarity)
why_retained_or_superseded: Captured semantic topic similarity between case facts (0.1955), substantially outperforming BM25 (0.1175).
failure_notes: Bi-encoders evaluate query and document representations independently without cross-attention token interaction, missing subtle statutory distinctions.

approach: TF-IDF N-Gram Retrieval Baseline with Cosine Similarity
why_retained_or_superseded: Stronger than vanilla BM25 due to legal n-gram phrase matching (0.1742 vs 0.1175).
failure_notes: High dimensional sparse vectors lacked semantic generalization for synonymous legal concepts.

approach: Bi-Encoder Dense Retriever trained with BM25 Hard Negatives
why_retained_or_superseded: Trained to discriminate confusing legal documents retrieved by BM25. Over-penalized relevant documents sharing incidental terminology.
failure_notes: Hard negative mining selected false negatives (relevant cases with differing surface phrasing), depressing test score.

approach: Okapi BM25 Pure Lexical Baseline
why_retained_or_superseded: Standard information retrieval baseline. Establishes the floor for lexical matching in legal case law.
failure_notes: Legal vocabulary mismatch problem: judges formulate identical legal doctrines using completely different words across jurisdictions.
